In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs The Chief
Secretary on 14 February, 2024

 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
 Order Sheet
 Wppil No. 106 of 2023
 In The Matter of Suo Moto Public Interest Litigation
 Versus
 The Chief Secretary & Others
14/02/2024 Heard Mr. Dheeraj Wankhede, learned counsel appears as
 Amicus Curiae.

Also heard Mr. Yashwant Singh Thakur, learned
 Additional Advocate General, appearing for the respondents No. 1, 4,
5 & 6/State and Mr. Praphulla N. Bharat, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Trivikram Nayak,
learned counsel, appearing for respondent No.2.

In compliance of the order dated 10.01.2024, the Collector, Bilaspur and the Member Secretary,
Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board (for short, the Board) have filed their respective
affidavits.

The Member Secretary in its affidavit states that some of the industries causing pollution in the
District of Bilaspur were issued notices under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act,
1981, Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and Environmental Pollution Act, 1986,
respectively.

He further states that stern the Board shall take stern action against the polluters and
violaters of the environment norms.

On 17.01.2024, a meeting was convened by the Collector,
Bilaspur, alongwith Additional District Magistrate, Bilaspur, Sub Divisional Magistrate (for short,
the Sdm), Takhtpur, Bilha, Regional Officer of the Board, Bilaspur, Assistant Mining Officer,
Bilaspur, representatives from the Rto, General Manager, Industries Department, Executive
Engineer, Csidc, representatives of Industrial Association, Sirgitti and General Secretary, District
Industrial Corporation, Bilaspur where the following directions were given:
"a) Industries should be closed and shut down if they are transporting raw materials
through trucks without covering them with tarpaulin.

Such trucks should also be
seized.

b) M/s Hirri Dolomite mines have submitted that they do not transport dolomite
through the Pendridih Bypass Road.

The Mining Department should take legal action against them if they are found to be transporting
dolomite through the Pendridih Bypass Road.

c) Csidc has been directed to submit a detailed action plan with regard to disposal of industrial
waste in a safe and scientific manner.

d) It was directed that a joint committee should be formed which would inspect the Pendridih
Bypass Road weekly.

The joint committee would comprise of Sdm Bilaspur, Additional
Commissioner, Nagar Palika Nigam Bilaspur, Health Officer, Nagar Palika Nigam, Bilaspur,
Regional Officer, Cecb, Bilaspur, Mining Inspector, Mining Department Bilaspur, representatives
of Rto, Bilaspuri General Manager of Csidc Bilaspur and General Manager of Dic Bilaspur.

e) Commissioner, Nagar Palika Nigam, Bilaspur, was directed to ensure that no waste shall be
dumped or burned illegally anywhere in Bilaspur.

He was also instructed to arrange for the cleaning
of the plants growing along the Pendridih Bypass Road.
f) Any vehicle found to be dumping waste in industrial area shall be seized immediately.

g) The representative of the mining department was directed to ensure that while transporting raw
materials/minerals through trucks, the name of transporter, mines/company name and the
transporting route details shall be affixed on the front of such trucks.

h) The submissions made in the affidavit filed by the Chief Secretary in Wppil-106/2023 should be
followed by every department.

i) Police administration and Rto Bilaspur are instructed to monitor such vehicles coming from
other districts which are not covered with tarpaulin.

j) Csidc representative informed that for disposal of hazardous waste generated from the
industries, an agreement has been formed with M/s Kesda Management and the industry is still
under construction, which is supposed to be completed in about 18 months.

They were directed that
till the construction is completed, waste generated from the industries shall be disposed by Nagar
Palik Nigam, Bilaspur., etc."

It has been further stated in the affidavit that in furtherance of the meeting held on 17/01/2024, a
joint committee
comprising

of Sdm Bilaspur, Additional Commissioner, Nagar Palika Nigam
Bilaspur, Health Officer, Nagar Palika Nigam, Bilaspur, Regional Officer, Cecb, Bilaspur, Mining
Inspector, Mining Department Bilaspur, representatives of Rto, Bilaspur: General Manager of
Csidc Bilaspur and General Manager of Dic Bilaspur

was constituted by Collector, Bilaspur vide
order dated 18/01/2024.

The said committee was tasked with weekly inspection of the concerned
areas handling of waste in the Sirgitti Industrial Area as well as monitoring and taking action

2 against trucks transporting raw materials without tarpaulin cover on the Pendridih Bypass Road

. 
And the said Joint Task Committee (for short, the JTC), during its inspection had caught around 20 trucks in January 2024 belonging to various industries which were plying raw materials and products without covering them with tarpaulin and commensurate notice was issued and penalty was levied on them as per law, further, in the month of February as many as around 59 trucks belonging to several industries were also caught and the detailed report/list containing the information of all these trucks was sent to the Collector, Bilaspur by letter dated 31/01/2024 and 06/02/2024 respectively.
The letter also contained the information regarding the Environmental Compensation (for short, the EC) imposed on the industries plying such trucks.

The total EC imposed on the industries plying such non covered trucks in the month of January 2024 is Rs.
3,15,000/- and Rs. 95,000/- for the month of February, 2024 respectively.

The Member Secretary of the Board further in the said affidavit states that the JTC had also undertaken surprise inspection of several industries on 03/02/2024 during which some of the industries therein were found to be flouting and violating environmental norms on the basis of which Panchnama was prepared and notices were issued to them accordingly.

The JTC had also conducted surprise inspections of some other industries as well on 08/02/2024 wherein notices were issued against them by CSIDC and the Regional Officer, of the Board, Bilaspur and they were requested to comply with the same failing which action would be taken.

The violators against whom action was taken during the inspection in the month of December and initial period of January,
2024, against them, through the respective orders, EC has been levied for causing pollution.

Total of 57 trucks were found to be transporting industrial raw materials without being covered with tarpaulin and the 11 industries to which those trucks belonged have been imposed a total EC of Rs.
2,52,500/-.

It has been further stated that in light of the inspections carried out by the JTC, several industries in the Bilaspur District were issued notices under the Air and Water Act and also Environmental Compensation was levied against them vide the notices dated between 7th-9th February, 2024.
The Municipal Corporation, Bilaspur through private entities is also regularly conducting the cleaning of Pendridih Bypass Road.

In furtherance of the objective to dispose the waste in a proper manner and to provide a clean environment, an MoU has been entered between the CSIDC and Nagar Palika Nigam on 29/01/2024 for proper disposal of waste.

A two-day workshop was also organized by the Collector, Bilaspur (Mining Department) from 07/02/2024 to 08/02/2024 which included representatives from the CECB and the of mines, workshop dealt with the aspect of environmental clearance of transportation of minerals and complying with environmental norms, etc. amongst other things.

Lastly, the Member Secretary of the Board states that the Board through its concerned officers shall continue to take action against violators and polluters with the help of the District Administration.

It is also submitted that in adequate cases complaint as envisaged under Section 43 of Air Act and/or 49 of Water Act would be filed against erring industries, persons, etc. in accordance with law as per the prescribed procedure.

He assured this Court that the Board shall abide by and comply with all the directions and orders passed by this Hon'ble High Court and also undertakes to take action against environmental polluters/violators as per law.

sentences.text: Similarly, the District Magistrate, Bilaspur, has also filed his affidavit in compliance of the order dated 10.01.2024 in which he has also made similar submissions as that of the Member Secretary of the Board.

In addition, he states that as per the instruction received in the meeting held on date 17/01/2024,
and agreement has been entered between Chhattisgarh State Industrial Development Corporation (CSIDC) Bilaspur and Nagar Palik Nigam, Bilaspur on date 26/01/2024.

entities.text: Chhattisgarh State Industrial Development Corporation (CSIDC) Bilaspur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The agreement aims to allow for the proper collection, segregation and disposal of the industrial waste generated by the industrial units identified by CSIDC, Bilaspur via M/s M.S.W. Solutions Limited, which is an agency have a valid contract with the Nagar Palik Nigam in this regard.

As per the agreement, the Memorandum of Understanding shall remain in force for a period of 03 months from 29/01/2024 and can also be extended through mutual consent after completion of the period of such terms.

The Nagar Palik Nigam shall be responsible for secondary collection, transportation of the segregated solid waste with (Segregation at source by the Generator) and processing of transported waste complying all Waste Management Rules, 2016 from CSIDC area.
In addition to the solid waste collected from the secondary transfer station, other wastes/legacy waste which will be transported by CSIDC to the processing site at Kachhar will be processed.

The said agreement aims for a proper,
total and scientific disposal of the waste generated by the industries in the Sirgitti area and aims to eradicate such occurrences of illegal waste dumping and burning.
In addition to the above, the joint inspection committee submitted its report to the Collector, Bilaspur on date 05/02/2024.
As per the joint inspection committee's report, the following steps/actions have been taken -
The illegal dumping area as well as the entire Sirgitti Industrial Area is being regularly inspected and monitored by the committee.

To spread awareness in this regard, the committee is convening meetings with the industrial union from time to time, installing notice boards and warning boards in appropriate places in the industrial area.
M/s Chhattisgarh Power and Coal Benefactions Limited, Sirgitti was inspected by the committee on date 01/02/2024.

entities.text: Chhattisgarh Power and Coal Benefactions Limited, Sirgitti
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the inspection, it was observed that there was no wheel washing system at the entry gate and the outer gate of the industry.
It was also observed that coal was stacked higher than the boundary wall of the industry and there was no garland drain around along the boundary of the industry.
In addition to this several other anomalies were also observed.

The Regional Officer,
Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board has imposed an Environmental Compensation of Rs. 30,000 on M/s Chhattisgarh Power and Coal Beneficiations Limited, Sirgitti by their letter dated 05/02/2024.

entities.text: Chhattisgarh Power and Coal Beneficiations Limited, Sirgitti
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The committee has also inspected the Pendridih Bypass Road from date 28/01/2024 to 30/01/2024.
During the inspection, 4 trucks were found plying without covering their raw material with tarpaulin.
These 4 trucks also did not have the TP pass for the materials they were transporting.
In addition to this, 20 trucks were found plying without covering their raw material with tarpaulin.
These 24 vehicles were seized.
A fine of Rs. 1,07,288 was imposed on the seized four vehicles and only after payment of such fine, the vehicles were released.

In addition to the above-mentioned actions, fencing and notice boards have been installed in the area which has been designated by the CSIDC for dumping of industrial waste in Sirgitti Industrial In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs The Chief Secretary on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281664/
4 Area.
Photographs of the same have been attached.
The flying squad of the RTO Bilaspur has Jointly inspected the Pendridih Bypass Road.

A total of 19 vehicles were found violating the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and a total fine of Rs.
44,000 have been imposed on such vehicles by the RTO Bilaspur.

A workshop regarding "Reappraisal of Environmental Clearance, compliance of mine safety and environmental norms and transportation of minerals" was conducted in the Manthan Sabhaghar,
Collector Office on dates 07/02/2024 and 08/02/2024 respectively.

In this workshop, the Regional Officer and Scientist, Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board, Bilaspur; Deputy Director,
Mining Department, Bilaspur and their officers; officers of RTO Bilaspur; coal storage license holders and mining lease holders were present.
It has been also stated that on 07/02/2024, the Director General of Mines Safety explained in detail about the solutions which should be implemented for safe operation of mining activities.
He discussed details regarding the height of the bench, how the slope should be, in which situations can the mining activities be stopped with immediate effect.
He also informed in detail about how to maintain the safety, health and well being of miners and what diseases could they possibly suffer from.

The Deputy Director, Mining Department and Regional Officer, Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board informed that the mine operators who have received Environmental Clearance from District Environment Impact Assessment Authority (DEIAA) in between the dates 15/01/2016 to 13/09/2018 have to mandatorily get their Environmental Clearance re- appraised by State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA).

entities.text: State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authority
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: They also informed the mine operators regarding the documents necessary for such appraisal.

On the second day of the workshop, that is 08/02/2024, the Scientist, Chhattisgarh Environment Conservation Board, Bilaspur informed that while loading and unloading coal in coal washeries,
there should be proper arrangement of water sprinkling systems for suppression any kind of dust emission.

A large pit filled with water should be created around the entry gate of such washeries,
which will absorb the coal dust and other particles from the truck tires.
It shall also be ensured that such trucks are properly covered with tarpaulin before letting them transport coal.
Such trucks should not be covered with green net.
The coal storage area should have proper water sprinkling system and adequate plantation.
As per the affidavit, the RTO officers have informed that trucks should not be overloaded while transporting coal/raw materials.
It shall also be ensured that the top of the vehicle is completely and securely covered with tarpaulin to prevent any and every kind of dust emission.
Old vehicles not having fitness certificate should not be used for transportation of raw materials as they emit much more pollution than other vehicles.
It should be ensured that all the vehicles engaged in mineral transportation have their respective vehicle fitness certificate.
Also, tail lights and reflectors of such vehicles should be properly maintained to prevent the instances of road accidents.

The Deputy Director, Mining Department, Bilaspur instructed to all coal storage license holders that they should install a board containing details regarding the licensee's name, validity of the license, area of the licensed place and amount of the mineral stored so that it is easier to ascertain the validity of such In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs The Chief Secretary on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6281664/
5 coal storage license holders.

He also instructed that the coal storage license holders should maintain a That, the efforts instrumentalities and the of the state joint inspection committee have also been recognized by print media.

Several news articles have been published in daily newspapers like Haribhoomi and Navbharat in the month of January, 2024 and February, 2024 which detail the stringent actions and steps taken by state instrumentalities and the joint inspection committee in compliance of the Hon'ble High Courts orders passed in WP (PIL) 106/2023.

It has lastly been stated that the authorities are taking positive efforts to curb the menace of waste dumping in the Sirgittin Industrial area and are also taking positive action with regard to cleaning of the Pendridih Bypass Road.

Learned Amicus Curiae has pointed out that though it appears that the State has taken action against the persons who are involved in violation of the Rules and Regulations prescribed under the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 (for short,
the Rules of 2016), but he states that what steps are required to be taken by the plants / industrial units in order to comply with the Rules of 2016, probably they are not aware of the said fact.

entities.text: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He places his reliance on the order of the the Supreme Court dated 10.07.2018 in re Outrage as Parents End Life After Childs Dengue passed in SMW (C) No.1/2015 wherein the State of Chhattisgarh was also imposed with a cost of Rs. 1,00,000/- for non compliance of the orders passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the directions issued by the Government of India.
Learned Advocate General states that they will take necessary steps with respect to the said Rules framed by the Central Government.

In view of the above, the District Magistrate, Bilaspur shall file a fresh affidavit as to what steps have been taken in pursuance of the Rules and Regulation prescribed under the Rules of 2016 and the order passed by the Apex Court as aforesaid.
Let the matter be listed after three weeks.
The learned State Counsel is directed to send a copy of this order to the District Magistrate, Bilaspur for necessary information and compliance forthwith.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Arvind Kumar Verma) (Ramesh Sinha)
